entries.notes: We are a lesbian-owned and operated business and carry the handcrafted work of over 150 women, including jewelry, pottery, batiks, toys, chairs, stained glass, planthangers, and much more. A 6 ft. Amazon carving guards our door. We're open May thru Oct. and possibly weekends until December. Come and see us when you're in Provincetown. Any lesbians with arts or crafts to sell or consign to a lesbian business, please write: Womencrafts, PO Box 190, Provincetown, MA, 02657. We need inexpensive things to sell to tourists as well as beautiful work especially for women.

I am doing a paper on "Gay Slang and the Issue of Community: Are You One, Too?" It will show how lesbian slang and humor differ from straight and gay male slang. The most important aspect that we intend to stress is its lack of personal derogation. Any suggestions, comments, jokes, or input of any kind should be sent to: Julia Stanley, Dept. of English, U. of N., Lincoln, Nebraska, 68588.

Conference at San Francisco State University, on Oct. 16 and 17 to explore the many kinds of violence in the lives of all women, and to seek possible solutions. For more info, write: Women's Center, SF State Student Union, 1600 Holloway, SF, CA, 94132 - Attn: Shoshana Rosenberg.

entries.notes: is scheduled to begin Sept. 13 through the 26th at the Cinema studio on Broadway at 66th St. In New York City. The Festival is designed to present a program of films directed by women. For more info, write: Festival of Women's Films, 36 W. 62nd St., NY, NY, 10023.

wimmin's bookstore at 2 Highland, Highland Park, MI, 48203, is now open Wed., Thurs., & Fri., 2-7 PM and Sun. Noon to 5. We stock books, music, and crafts by, for and about wimmin. We also have discussion groups and music and poetry sharing. Stop in or call 869-4045.

The oppression of native peoples stretches far. Women have been and still are a strong force fighting for native American sovereignty. These women are ignored by the media in their confrontation and struggle with the FBI. We must learn about and support these women. For general info, write: Women Supporting Native American Sovereignty, c/o Mother Kali's Bookstore, 333 W. 11th, Eugene, OR, 97401.

Are you a Philadelphia womon who is Jewish? If so, come to our Friday night services. Services will be starting in Sept. All women welcome. We are a totally non-sexist, women's synagogue, trying to make Judaism relate to our feminism. Write: Congregation Beth Ishah, c/o Sarak Revinsky, 643 Ritner St., Philadelphia, PA, 19148 - Phone HO - 5 - 2605.
